sections.html:
Macrognathus taeniagaster is a small spiny eel from Thailand. It can change colour very fast: the same fish can be uniformly beige in one moment and in the next show an almost white back and a dark belly.

Lexicon: Macrognathus is ancient Greek and means "with big jaw"; taeniagaster is ancient Greek and means "with banded belly"; circumcinctus is Latin and means "girdled thorough".

Basically speaking, the spiny eels of Asia can be divided in two groups: the small species belonging to the genus Macrognathus that usually reach only 10-15 cm total length and the large species of the genus Mastacembelus that grow to more than 40 cm (maximum length reported: 100 cm).
Keeping these spiny eels is very easy. The fish like the company of their own kind and often share the same hiding place.
Macrognathus feed readily on any type of frozen and live fish food. Very small fish are taken as food.
In general the spiny eels are very peaceful towards tankmates and are very suitable for community tanks.
Males stay smaller than the females and are much more slim.
The fish spawn near the water surface in the roots of floating fern and similar plants. It is possible to breed these fish in aquaria, but this is rarely done.
